title: Why Does Ice Float?
subject: Physics
objective: Most solids sink in their own liquid, but ice floats. How open hexagons make ice less dense, and why that keeps lakes alive.

fill.q: A solid floats if it is ____ dense than the liquid.
In ice, water molecules form open ____.
On freezing, water's volume grows by about ____ percent.

tf.q: Most solids sink in their own liquid.
Ice has less mass than the water it came from.

tf.explain: Ethanol is less dense than ice.

ar.r: Ice is less dense than water.

ar.a: Water pipes can burst in winter.

mcq.q: Ice is less dense than water because:
About how much of an iceberg is under water?
Fish survive under a frozen lake because:

num.q: A floating block has density 0.8 in a liquid of density 1.0. What percent is under the surface?
Density of a 10 g object with volume 5 cm³, in g/cm³?

short.q: Why does solid wax sink in liquid wax but ice float on water?
short.solution: Solid wax is denser than liquid wax. Ice is less dense than water, because freezing locks molecules into open hexagons.
